name: index
description: Build the code index. Call it only when a tool says "No codebase indexed". Pass an absolute path, or comma-separated paths for a monorepo. A file watcher then keeps it fresh.

name: search
description: Find code by meaning or keyword: "where is...", "how does... work", "find the code that...". Returns ranked results with file and line range; the first three carry the whole function or class. Exact names in the query (`parse_config RetryPolicy`) bring their definitions first. For the full code of a cut result, call `find_symbol`.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: What to find, in plain words or code terms

name: find_symbol
description: Get the whole code of functions, classes, methods or constants by name ("show me create_order"), with file, line range, callers and callees. Use it instead of a file read or grep for a definition. Pass several names in one call. A class over 2,000 characters gives an outline; ask for "Class.method" for one method. For every use of a name, use `graph`.

arguments.name: symbol_name
arguments.desc: One name, or several with commas

arguments.name: exact
arguments.desc: False matches part of a name

name: graph
description: Trace the call graph: who calls a function (direction='callers') or what it calls ('callees'). transitive=true covers everything that depends on it; use it before you change, rename or delete a shared function ("what breaks if I change X"). A callers result also has `references`, the whole-word uses of the name, so no grep is needed. For a method, pass `Class.method`: the result also lists the `overrides` in subclasses. Edges are static: calls through callbacks, reflection or dynamic dispatch show only in `references`.

arguments.name: transitive
arguments.desc: All direct and indirect dependents. Only with direction='callers'.

name: map
description: Get an overview of the project: "give me an overview", "how is this structured", "where do I start". 'summary' lists files, languages, top modules and quality. 'architecture' gives layers, dependencies, entry points and hub symbols. 'full' gives both. Use it first in an unfamiliar repository.
